newsitem.title: USA: Little change in Sino-US status after Deng -USDA.
newsitem.headline: Little change in Sino-US status after Deng -USDA.

text.p: Little change was likely in Sino-U.S. agricultural trade relations with the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, an advisor to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Wednesday.

The nations are in dispute over several issues, including access for U.S. farm exports to China's market and reforms needed for Beijing to join the World Trade Organization. China is a major customer for U.S. farm goods.
"I wouldn't think it (Deng's death) would have much impact," said Paul Drazek, trade advisor to Glickman, but he added it was too early to tell with certainty.
